# Your money is stuck. You deserve answers.

*By Inês, Product Designer at Pinha · 10 November 2026*

Since Friday, 6 November, you have not been able to withdraw your money from Pinha. Our payments partner, Northvale Payments, blocked all outgoing transfers at 09:00 that morning without warning. Deposits and round-ups have also stopped.

**Your money has not been lost. It remains in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own money, and Northvale cannot use it for its own purposes. But we cannot move it until Northvale releases it.**

That distinction matters. So does this: money you cannot access cannot pay your rent, cover a prescription or meet a deadline. Saying it is safeguarded does not make being locked out of it acceptable.

We are angry at Northvale. We are also responsible for choosing a setup that left you dependent on one partner, with no backup. You are entitled to be angry with them and with us.

Here is what happened, what we are doing and what you can do now.

## If you need your money urgently

**If this freeze is affecting rent, medical costs or your ability to manage after losing your job, email urgent@pinha.example with the subject line URGENTE.** Tell us what you need the money for and whether there is a deadline.

We are trying to secure individual releases for urgent cases. We cannot guarantee that Northvale will agree, or how quickly it will act. I wish we could give you something firmer. For now, this is the route we have for raising those cases.

Our support team has received 1,900 emails since Friday. There are three people answering them, and replies are currently taking around two days. That is a long time to wait when the question is about your own money. The urgent address helps us identify the cases where waiting could cause the most immediate harm; it is not a promise of an immediate release.

**We have cancelled Pinha’s monthly fee for November and December for everyone.** You do not need to ask us to do this.

## What Northvale did

Northvale Payments is an electronic money institution based in Vilnius. It is the partner that holds Pinha customers’ money.

On **4 November**, Northvale emailed us a notice of “commercial termination”, giving 30 days’ notice. The explanation it provided was a “risk appetite review”. We have not been given a more specific reason.

On **6 November at 09:00**, just two days later, Northvale blocked all outgoing transfers without warning. That was not the 30-day transition its notice had set out. Deposits and round-ups stopped too.

This left you unable to withdraw your savings and left us unable to move them for you.

On **7 November**, we filed complaints with Banco de Portugal and the Lithuanian central bank. Rui, our CEO, is working with our lawyers and speaking with Banco de Portugal about getting your money moving again.

We are challenging Northvale’s actions. But a complaint is not the same as a release of funds, and we will not pretend that filing one has fixed anything.

## Where your money is

Customer money is held in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own funds. It is not money Northvale can use to run its business.

**The problem is access: the money remains safeguarded, but it is currently blocked.** Pinha cannot bypass that block or transfer the money out ourselves.

We want to be precise about this because “your money is safe” can sound like “there is nothing to worry about”. There is plenty to worry about when you need your savings and cannot reach them. Safeguarding matters, but it does not resolve the situation you are in today.

## What needs to happen next

We have already signed with a new partner: **Ostra Bank, based in Lisbon**.

To migrate, we need Northvale to send the balances file—the record of customers’ balances needed for the transfer—and we need Banco de Portugal’s approval. Signing with Ostra is an important step, but it does not remove either of those dependencies.

Our current estimate for the migration is **10 to 15 working days**. **That is an estimate, not a confirmed withdrawal date.** It depends on steps we do not control, and we cannot promise when you will regain access.

We are sharing that estimate because you deserve to know what we are working towards, not because we want you to plan a rent payment or another commitment around an unconfirmed date.

If the estimate changes, we will say so. If something is still blocked, we will say what is blocking it.

## Our mistake

We chose Northvale. We relied on a single payments partner. We did not have a backup ready that could keep your money accessible if that relationship failed.

That was our mistake.

Northvale is responsible for its decision to block transfers. We are responsible for the dependence we built into Pinha. Both things are true, and pointing to Northvale does not let us step away from our part.

I am Pinha’s product designer. I write many of the words you see in the app, and I designed the screen that says:

“Your money is always yours, take it out anytime.”

I look at that sentence now and feel sick. You cannot do what we told you that you could do. I helped make that promise, and I owe you an acknowledgement of how badly it has failed you.

One person wrote to us about saving for three years for a car deposit. The dealer’s deadline is this Friday, 13 November. I read that message on the metro and nearly cried.

My feelings do not help her meet that deadline. I mention the message because this is what is in our inbox: people who have saved, made plans and relied on being able to use their own money. There is no reassuring phrase that makes that okay.

I am sorry we put you in this position. You do not owe us patience, and I am not going to ask you to calm down.

## What you can expect from us

We will publish an update **every Monday and Thursday on this blog until this is resolved**. The next scheduled update is **Thursday, 12 November**.

Those updates will explain what has moved, what is still blocked and whether our estimate has changed. If we have no progress to report, we will say that rather than leave you wondering whether we have gone quiet.

For now:

- **For urgent cases involving rent, medical costs or job loss:** email **urgent@pinha.example**, with **URGENTE** in the subject line, and explain your situation and any deadline.
- **For other support questions:** our current reply time is around **two days**.
- **For progress updates:** check this blog every **Monday and Thursday**.
- **For monthly fees:** November and December are cancelled for everyone, with no action needed from you.

You should not have to chase a savings app to get access to your savings. Until you can withdraw your money again, this is not resolved.

Inês
